name: Villarreal CF

identity.playing_style: Marcelino's 2025/26 Villarreal were a disciplined 4-4-2 counter-attacking side that finished 3rd, overtaking Atlético with a 5-1 final-day win, with Georges Mikautadze scoring 13 league goals. Iñigo Pérez (appointed 1 June 2026) arrives from Rayo Vallecano, where he took a low-budget squad to the Conference League final with an intense, front-foot pressing 4-4-2/4-2-3-1; expect higher pressing volume than under Marcelino.
principles: academy-first (Ciudad Deportiva, one of Spain's most productive)
identity.club_character: Town of ~50k with a family-owned, patient, low-drama club culture; expectations calibrated to Europe every year rather than titles; minimal media pressure compared with Madrid/Barcelona.
identity.ownership: Private, family-owned: Fernando Roig (ceramics industrialist) since 1997
identity.political_and_social_context: Publicly documented: club's long-standing public stance in favour of Spanish clubs' economic-control model and against the Super League project; Fernando Roig's public criticism of La Liga scheduling/refereeing decisions. No further institution-level controversies verified for 2025/26.
identity.wage_structure: flat-to-moderate; strictly within La Liga salary-cap limits
identity.transfer_policy: very quiet summer 2026: only one signing (Andero Kaares, youth) per Transfermarkt-based reports; outgoings mostly loans (Pedraza to Lazio, Conde to Mallorca, Requena to Betis) plus Terrats sold to Getafe for EUR 2.5m; net +EUR 2.5m

last_season_2025_26.ucl_result: League phase participant (final ranking/elimination not verified)

strengths: Third in La Liga two seasons in a row, finishing above Atlético in 2025/26.
Squad continuity: almost no senior departures, so Pérez inherits an intact core.
Mikautadze (13 league / 15 total goals) is a reliable primary scorer.
Strong academy pipeline continuously supplies first-team-ready players.
weaknesses: Only one (youth) signing all summer: a squad that finished 3rd has not been strengthened for a double campaign.
Coaching change from Marcelino's counter-attacking 4-4-2 to Pérez's pressing game requires adaptation mid-season.
Early Copa del Rey exit (round of 32) and unverified Champions League 2025/26 outcome suggest cup/European inconsistency.
Loss of Pedraza (loan) thins left-back cover behind returning Carlos Romero.

positional_needs.reason: Terrats sold and Requena loaned; Pérez's system demands midfield running

positional_needs.profile: athletic full-back able to press high

positional_needs.reason: depth behind Mikautadze for UCL and league
